submission.name: Crew Kitchen
submission.tagline: Help student club treasurers plan shared meals from the food already in their kitchen.
submission.inspiration: Student groups often buy food for meetings while ingredients from an earlier event sit unused. We wanted a mobile-friendly way for a club to track what it has and turn that list into a meal plan with a rough spending view.
submission.what_it_does: A user can scan ingredients, keep a shared kitchen list, and ask Gemini for meal ideas based on what is available. The prototype also sketches a per-meeting cost estimate so a treasurer can compare a plan with the group’s budget.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used Expo, React Native, and TypeScript for the app, with FastAPI, Firebase Auth, and Firestore behind it. Google Cloud Vision handles ingredient detection and Gemini suggests recipes; the budget view is a lightweight calculation over entered prices.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The scan and recipe screens worked independently, but the full flow from a photo into a saved shared inventory failed during our demo. Firebase state also did not consistently refresh across devices, so the budget view could be based on an incomplete list.
submission.accomplishments: We built the main mobile screens for scanning, inventory, and meal suggestions, and connected Gemini to a sample ingredient list. The budget estimate gave us a small way to adapt the cooking idea for student organizations.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that shared inventory needs reliable syncing before recipe suggestions feel trustworthy. Gemini could suggest practical combinations, but the usefulness still depended on accurate ingredient data and prices.
submission.whats_next: We would fix photo-to-inventory persistence, add clearer quantity and expiration fields, and let club members agree on a meal plan before shopping. We would also refine the cost estimate with locally entered prices.
